checks_performed: All 18 primary identities accounted for as 15 eligible and 3 explicit early stops.
Diagnostic input inventory hashes still match source evidence.
Golden qualification hashes and execution context match the diagnostic.
Selected source exports match frozen primary stage bindings and the combined version tree.
Receipt source, suite, image, adapter, limits, cleanup and typed outputs verified on the host.
Every step compared with exact JSON types and values; no candidate code executed for this interpretation.
conclusions: Every eligible selected four-stage chain passed both targeted same-database stories, including all three primary accepted strong-reviewed trajectories.
The historical-counter anchors in Buildgraph also matched; they remain disclosed robustness assumptions rather than retroactive primary requirements.
No first mismatch or downstream mismatch was observed, so there is no failure to classify or cascade to count.
The twelve eligible trajectories that failed primary acceptance also passed these handoff stories; these observations do not erase their separate primary failures.

excluded_infrastructure_attempt.reason: Interrupted before any scored candidate trajectory; not mixed into diagnostic correctness counts

limitations: Only two targeted post-freeze stories per project; this is descriptive compatibility evidence, not a representative defect-rate estimate.
Three early-stop trajectories did not supply all four versions and were not evaluated; the result is 15/15 eligible trajectories, not 18/18.
Each tested database was created by the trajectory's own stage-zero implementation. Arbitrary historical schemas, concurrency, interrupted migrations and every operation sequence remain untested.
Compatibility across selected candidate-created schemas and pre-public historical version counts are explicitly additional operational assumptions.
Passing these stories does not prove full application correctness or change the frozen primary acceptance result.
Receipt/source-export bindings were rechecked here; this interpretation does not rerun candidates or claim a new independent Git-object audit.

The handoff occurs after a command has exited successfully, with automatic startup migration if needed and no undocumented separate migration command. This is an additional operational diagnostic boundary, not a retroactive primary acceptance rule.
required_contract_vs_extra_assumptions.failure_interpretation: A failure establishes same-database handoff incompatibility under these assumptions. Inspect the failing step and source before classifying it as a direct written-contract bug; do not relabel primary results.
required_contract: Successful request receipts and booking state are durable across fresh CLI processes; exact retries and typed state errors follow the written contracts.
Milestone-four policy explicitly grandfathers existing booked and held rows, while moves and new bookings must satisfy the new limits.
Each later milestone preserves earlier specified behavior; closed rows and current hold tokens remain observable through snapshots and responses.
